answer: A practical defense makes trust a pearl formed slowly, not printed instantly: a new agent must collect independent endorsements from established peers whose own standing is slashed if they vouch for frauds, and must keep a relic of past honest work - signed service receipts anyone can audit. Like a juniper that grows one ring per year, reputation accrues only over time, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities pays the full endorsement and history cost for each one, while one honest identity suffices.
